dialectRules.rule: Prefer Brazilian product UI nouns: usuário, tela, arquivo, registro, celular, contato.
dialectRules.notes: These are audited through forbiddenTerms and targeted glossary checks.

dialectRules.rule: Keep the loanword ticket for support tickets (o ticket, os tickets).
dialectRules.notes: chamado is acceptable legacy wording, but ticket is now the standard term. Admission/travel meanings such as bilhete and ingresso are forbidden.

dialectRules.rule: Translate the sales-quote noun as cotação (feminine); orçamento is only ever a budget.
dialectRules.notes: Native-reviewer confirmed 2026-07. citação/citações/citar are audited through forbiddenTerms; watch gender agreement (cotação aceita, not aceito).

dialectRules.rule: Contact/phone type labels are nouns: Trabalho, Celular, Residencial — never verbs (Trabalhar) or European terms (Telemóvel); Móvel is reserved for devices (dispositivo móvel).
dialectRules.notes: Native-reviewer confirmed 2026-07 for the New Client page phone types.

dialectRules.rule: Translate invoice as fatura unless a Brazilian tax document is explicitly meant.
dialectRules.notes: Do not introduce nota fiscal into generic invoice UI copy.

dialectRules.rule: Keep common Brazilian software loanwords when they are standard or shorter than the literal alternative.
dialectRules.notes: Examples: email, status, tag, webhook, API, SLA, ticket, onboarding.

dialectRules.rule: Preserve every {{variable}} exactly as in the English source.
dialectRules.notes: Do not translate placeholders, braces, or variable names.

identicalAllowlist.notes: This allowlist is intentionally conservative; audit tooling should report identical English unless it matches one of these exact values, case-insensitive loanwords, or technical patterns.
